neighbours.label: the opening quotation mark of a quoted motto, saying or slogan (the old adage “…, his tagline “…)
fire: My grandmother lived by the old proverb “waste not, want not” all her life.
The school motto, “Learn to serve,” is carved above the main door.
We all know the saying “practice makes perfect,” but few of us follow it.
The brand's famous slogan “Just do it” first appeared in 1988.
Remember the old adage “better safe than sorry” when you hike alone.
The campaign used the catchy tagline “Every vote counts” on all its posters.
Her favourite maxim, “Less is more,” guided every room she designed.
The club's motto “Never give up” is printed on the back of every shirt.
quiet: My grandmother looked at me and said “come inside, it's raining” before dinner.
The head teacher asked, “Who left the door open?” at the morning assembly.
We all heard him shout “stop the car,” but nobody reacted in time.
The customer told the waiter “I ordered tea” when the coffee arrived.
My friend texted me “running late” just before the hike started.
The volunteer at the desk replied “Room four” when we asked for the meeting.
Her client phoned and said “The paint is too dark” about the living room.
The coach yelled “Get back on defence” from the side of the pitch.

notes: Card: ' "' x9 and ' “' x8 after adage/motto/saying/tagline; output suppresses opening quote marks. Near misses open ordinary reported speech.
